title: Personal Finance: Money for Life
tagline: Budget your salary, build an emergency fund, use credit wisely, avoid debt traps and start investing, Dubai-style.

superpower.name: Money Wise
superpower.description: Budgets and saves like a pro: steadier wallet and fewer money worries.

syllabus: Week 2: Saving and the emergency fund
Week 3: Credit cards, loans and your credit score
Week 4: Investing, compounding and avoiding scams

weeks.title: Budgeting
weeks.objective: Know where every dirham goes, and give it a job.

slides.title: The 50/30/20 Budget
slides.body: A simple starting budget splits take-home pay into needs, wants and savings. In Dubai, rent often takes more than people expect, so adjust the split to your reality.
bullets: 50% needs: rent, bills, food, transport
30% wants: eating out, shopping, trips
20% savings and debt repayment
Track spending for a month before you set limits
slides.example:
Take-home salary: AED 12,000 a month.
Needs (50%): AED 6,000, for rent of AED 4,000, bills, groceries and Metro.
Wants (30%): AED 3,600.
Savings (20%): AED 2,400 a month, AED 28,800 a year.
slides.takeaway: A budget isn't a cage: it's permission to spend without guilt.

slides.title: Fixed and Flexible Costs
slides.body: Fixed costs (rent, phone plan, school fees) stay the same each month; flexible ones (food, fun) change. Cutting a big fixed cost once saves every month.
bullets: Share a flat or move further out to cut rent
Review phone, gym and streaming subscriptions
Cook more; delivery fees add up
Use the Metro and Nol card where possible
slides.takeaway: Cut big fixed costs first: one decision, savings forever.

lab.title: Budget Lab
lab.brief: Track a month of spending (real or in-game), sort it into needs, wants and savings, and write next month's budget.
lab.deliverable: A spending table and a new budget.
lab.proTip: Automate savings on payday: what you don't see, you don't spend.

caseStudy.scenario: You earn AED 9,000 and spend AED 9,200 every month. What's the best first step?

options.text: Take a credit card to cover the gap.
Track every expense, then cut the biggest costs to spend less than you earn.
options.explanation: Spending less than you earn is the foundation.
Small gaps grow into big debts.

quiz.question: A fixed cost is:
quiz.explanation: Rent stays the same each month.

weeks.title: Saving and the Emergency Fund
weeks.objective: Build a safety net so a surprise doesn't become a crisis.

slides.title: Your Emergency Fund
slides.body: Life happens: job loss, medical bills, car repairs. An emergency fund of 3 to 6 months of essential costs means you can handle it without debt. For expats, losing a job can also mean visa deadlines, so a fund matters even more.
bullets: Target: 3 to 6 months of essential spending
Keep it in a separate savings account you can reach quickly
Only for true emergencies
Rebuild it after you use it
slides.example:
Essential costs: AED 7,000 a month.
Target: 3 to 6 months = AED 21,000 to AED 42,000.
Saving AED 1,500 a month, you reach AED 21,000 in 14 months.
slides.takeaway: An emergency fund turns a crisis into an inconvenience.

slides.title: Saving Habits
slides.body: Saving works best on autopilot: pay yourself first, the day salary lands.
bullets: Standing order to savings on payday
Name your goals: 'Emergency', 'Holiday', 'Car deposit'
Save windfalls: half of any bonus straight to savings
Compare savings rates between banks
slides.takeaway: Pay yourself first, then live on the rest.

lab.title: Emergency Fund Lab
lab.brief: Calculate your 3 and 6 month targets and set up an automatic monthly saving plan to reach one.
lab.deliverable: Your targets and a dated savings plan.
lab.proTip: Start small: even AED 300 a month builds the habit.

caseStudy.scenario: Your car needs a AED 4,000 repair and you have no savings. What would an emergency fund have prevented?

options.text: Borrowing on a credit card at high interest to pay for it.
options.explanation: With a fund you pay cash and avoid expensive debt.
It doesn't stop repairs, it pays for them.

weeks.title: Credit and Debt
weeks.objective: Use credit as a tool, never a trap.

slides.title: Credit Cards and Interest
slides.body: Credit cards are useful if you pay the full balance every month. If you don't, interest is charged monthly and compounds fast; UAE card rates are often around 3% a month, more than 36% a year.
bullets: Pay the full statement balance every month
The 'minimum payment' mostly pays interest
Cash withdrawals on cards cost fees and interest immediately
Buy now, pay later is still debt: count it in your budget
slides.example:
A AED 10,000 card balance at about 3% a month:
Paying only the minimum, you might pay around AED 300 a month in interest alone.
That's about AED 3,600 a year for nothing.
slides.takeaway: Only buy on credit what you could buy with cash today.

slides.title: Your Credit Score
slides.body: The Al Etihad Credit Bureau (AECB) keeps credit reports and scores (from 300 to 900) for UAE residents. Banks check them for cards, loans and even some rentals and jobs.
bullets: Pay every bill and instalment on time
Keep card usage low compared with your limit
Don't apply for lots of credit at once
Check your AECB report for mistakes
slides.takeaway: A good score means cheaper loans and more choices.

lab.title: Debt Plan Lab
lab.brief: List all debts with balances and interest rates, then make an avalanche plan (highest rate first) and a snowball plan (smallest balance first).
lab.proTip: The avalanche saves the most money; the snowball builds motivation. Either beats doing nothing.

caseStudy.scenario: You have two debts: a card at 36% a year and a car loan at 4%. You have AED 2,000 extra. Where should it go?

options.text: The credit card: it's the most expensive debt.
options.explanation: Paying the highest rate first saves the most.

options: Pay the full balance each month

weeks.title: Investing and Scams
weeks.objective: Grow your money over time and keep it safe from scammers.

slides.title: Compounding and Investing
slides.body: Money grows faster when its growth also grows: compounding. Time matters more than timing, so starting early is the biggest advantage.
bullets: Rule of 72: years to double ≈ 72 ÷ yearly return
Diversify: index funds spread risk across many companies
Invest only money you won't need for 5 years or more
Fees matter: a 1% fee takes a big bite over decades
slides.example:
AED 1,000 a month invested at 7% a year:
• After 10 years: about AED 173,000 (AED 120,000 put in)
• After 30 years: about AED 1.2 million (AED 360,000 put in)
The extra came from compounding.
slides.takeaway: Start early, spread risk, keep fees low, stay patient.

slides.title: Spotting Scams
slides.body: Scammers target savers with promises of easy returns. If it sounds too good to be true, it is.
bullets: Guaranteed high returns ('20% a month, no risk') are a lie
Pressure to decide now, or to keep it secret, is a red flag
Never share OTPs, card PINs or passwords: banks never ask
Check investment firms are licensed by the UAE regulators before investing
slides.takeaway: No real investment is guaranteed, urgent and secret.

lab.title: Investment Plan Lab
lab.brief: Use the Rule of 72 and a compounding table to compare investing AED 500 a month from age 22 and from age 35.
lab.deliverable: A comparison table and three lessons.
lab.proTip: The best time to start was yesterday; the next best is today.

caseStudy.scenario: A stranger on Instagram offers a 'guaranteed 15% a month' crypto plan if you send money today. What do you do?

options.text: Send a small amount to test it.
options.explanation: Scams often pay small amounts first to hook you.

options.text: Refuse, block and report it: guaranteed high returns are a scam sign.
options.explanation: Guaranteed, urgent, too-good returns are classic fraud.

options.text: Send your card details so they can 'verify' you.
options.explanation: Never share card details or OTPs.

A red flag for a scam is:
options: Guaranteed high returns and pressure to act now
quiz.explanation: Guarantees and pressure are warning signs.
